gloss: to carry on one's back; to shoulder (a burden)

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {背負|せお}っていませんでした

definitions.explanation: To physically carry something (a backpack, a child, etc.) on one's back. Compound of 背 (back) + 負う (to bear).

definitions.gloss: to shoulder; to bear (a responsibility, debt, burden)
definitions.explanation: To take on or bear a heavy responsibility, debt, or emotional burden. A common figurative extension of the physical meaning.

examples.japanese: リュックを{背負|せお}って{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I went out carrying a backpack.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}は{赤|あか}ちゃんを{背負|せお}って{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: My mother went shopping carrying the baby on her back.

examples.japanese: {重|おも}い{荷物|にもつ}を{背負|せお}って{山|やま}を{登|のぼ}った。
examples.english: I climbed the mountain carrying heavy baggage on my back.

examples.japanese: {借金|しゃっきん}を{背負|せお}っている。
{一人|ひとり}で{全|すべ}ての{責任|せきにん}を{背負|せお}う{必要|ひつよう}はない。
examples.english: You don't need to shoulder all the responsibility alone.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{家族|かぞく}の{期待|きたい}を{背負|せお}って、{試合|しあい}に{臨|のぞ}んだ。
examples.english: He entered the match bearing the expectations of his family.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Godan verb (う ending, conjugates as w-row: {背負|せお}わない, {背負|せお}います). Transitive — takes を.

USAGE:
The figurative sense (shouldering responsibility/burden) is extremely common and often more frequent in everyday use than the physical sense. Also read as しょう in literary contexts ({背負|しょ}う), though せおう is the standard modern pronunciation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {責任|せきにん}を{背負|せお}う (to shoulder responsibility)
- {借金|しゃっきん}を{背負|せお}う (to bear debt)
- リュックを{背負|せお}う (to carry a backpack)
- {十字架|じゅうじか}を{背負|せお}う (to bear one's cross)
- {運命|うんめい}を{背負|せお}う (to bear one's fate)
